answer: tools/bench/tournament.py schedules round-robin when n<=8 and the pair budget allows (round-robin), Swiss when the field is large (swiss), and elimination only when the budget cannot afford Swiss (elimination). The planted three-cycle [['wf-cycle-a', 'wf-cycle-b', 'wf-cycle-c']] is reported as ranking_kind=PARTIAL_ORDER with binding_leaderboard=null. Round-robin and Swiss agree on wf-apex on the transitive control and disagree on the unstable four-candidate field; that disagreement is schedule-finding schedule-disagreement with binding_top=null, not resolved by picking a scheduler. Full pairwise matrices are in pairwise_result_matrix below.

question: Build the tournament scheduler (round-robin for small fields, Swiss for large, elimination only where budget forces it) and test the resulting ranking for pairwise transitivity. Non-transitive results mean a single-number ranking is fiction and the field must be reported as a partial order.

residual_unknowns.claim: Live bucket-B04 workflow candidates are not on disk in this worktree. The scheduler and transitivity check were proven on synthetic wf-* fixtures that encode the required controls (planted cycle, transitive order, schedule-unstable field). A later unit that lands the B04 registry can feed those ids through evaluate_field without changing the comparison rule.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: When command-center/bench/cases/ contains real B04 candidate scores, re-run evaluate_field on that corpus and publish the pairwise matrix the same way.

residual_unknowns.claim: Swiss pairing here is deterministic adjacent-score pairing with name tie-break, not FIDE Dutch pairing. Whether a published-rating Swiss would change the unstable-field finding is not measured.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Swap _swiss_pair_round for Dutch pairing and re-run probe2.

reviewer.scope_not_agreement: probe2 recomputes winners and effect sizes (win-margin / n_cases) without calling pairwise_matrix or enumerate_cycles
